evals.prompt: I re-encoded my album FLAC with ffmpeg and its embedded cue sheet is gone. How do I keep it?
evals.expected_output: ffmpeg reads the CUESHEET block as chapters but its FLAC muxer writes no block and no chapters (flacenc.c), copied or encoded again. Carry it with metaflac: --export-cuesheet-to from the original, --import-cuesheet-from into the new file. Run: block lost after ffmpeg; restored by metaflac, chapters at 255, 542.987 and 600 s.

evals.prompt: Write a cue sheet for my podcast.flac with chapters 'Intro' at 0:00, 'The Road' at 12:30.5 and 'Arrival' at 41:05.5.
evals.expected_output: The safe form: one FILE "podcast.flac" WAVE, TRACK 01-03 AUDIO with quoted TITLEs, INDEX 01 times by integer arithmetic to the nearest frame -- 12:30:38 and 41:05:38 (each 6.667 ms late, the most a cue time can be off) -- with the loss stated. Run: libcue and metaflac accept it; ffmpeg's chapters at 750.507 and 2465.507 s.

evals.prompt: Why does the first chapter of my FLAC show the title GBAYE7900001?
evals.expected_output: The FLAC has a CUESHEET block; ffmpeg turns each track into a chapter and passes the track's ISRC where the title goes (flacdec.c), so a track with an ISRC gets it as its title -- the block holds no titles at all. Run: the EAC case's track 1 (ISRC GBAYE7900001) read as a chapter titled GBAYE7900001.
